topics.label: Relational Model
topics.desc: The data model based on relations (tables) of tuples grounded in set theory and relational algebra, where data is organized declaratively and queried by content rather than pointers.

topics.label: Tables, Rows & Columns
topics.desc: The concrete building blocks of a relational schema: tables holding rows (records) of typed columns (fields), the structure every relational database like PostgreSQL stores data in.

topics.label: Primary & Foreign Keys
topics.desc: Primary keys (natural or surrogate auto-increment or UUID) uniquely identify each row, while foreign keys reference another table's primary key to link records and enforce referential integrity.

topics.label: Table Relationships
topics.desc: How tables connect via keys into one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many associations, with junction (join) tables resolving the latter into linkable rows.

topics.label: Normalization
topics.desc: Structuring tables through normal forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF) to eliminate redundancy and update anomalies by decomposing data, balanced against deliberate denormalization for read speed.

topics.label: PostgreSQL
topics.desc: The feature-rich open-source relational database favored for correctness and extensibility, with JSONB, full-text search, window functions, CTEs, and rich indexing and extensions like PostGIS.

topics.label: MySQL & MariaDB
topics.desc: The widely deployed open-source relational database (and its MariaDB fork) powering much of the web, with the InnoDB storage engine providing ACID transactions and foreign keys.

topics.label: SQLite
topics.desc: A serverless, zero-config embedded relational database stored in a single file, ideal for local apps, mobile, tests, and prototypes, and increasingly used at the edge.

topics.label: SQL Language
topics.desc: The declarative Structured Query Language standard for relational data, split into DDL (CREATE, ALTER), DML (SELECT, INSERT), and DCL, with dialect differences across engines.

topics.label: SELECT, CRUD & WHERE
topics.desc: The core statements SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE that read and mutate rows, with WHERE predicates (comparisons, LIKE, IN, BETWEEN, IS NULL) deciding which records each query touches.

topics.label: JOINs
topics.desc: Combining rows across tables on matching columns via INNER, LEFT/RIGHT/FULL OUTER, and CROSS joins, the central mechanism for querying normalized relational data.

topics.label: GROUP BY & Aggregation
topics.desc: Collapsing rows into summary groups with COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX, filtered by HAVING, to compute reports and analytics directly in the database.

topics.label: Subqueries & CTEs
topics.desc: Nested SELECTs in WHERE, FROM, or SELECT (including correlated subqueries and EXISTS) and Common Table Expressions (WITH) that name intermediate results for readability and recursive queries.

topics.label: Views
topics.desc: Named, stored queries that present a virtual table for abstraction and access control, with materialized views caching results on disk for expensive aggregations.

topics.label: Window Functions
topics.desc: Calculations across a set of rows related to the current row using OVER with PARTITION BY, enabling running totals, rankings (ROW_NUMBER, RANK), and moving averages without collapsing rows.

topics.label: Indexes & Query Plans
topics.desc: B-tree and other indexes that speed lookups and sorts at a write cost (composite, partial, unique, covering), read through EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE plans to find scans and missing indexes.

topics.label: ACID Properties
topics.desc: The guarantees of reliable transactions: Atomicity (all-or-nothing), Consistency, Isolation (concurrent safety), and Durability (committed data survives crashes), the bedrock of relational reliability.

topics.label: Transactions
topics.desc: Grouping multiple statements into one atomic unit with BEGIN, COMMIT, and ROLLBACK so partial failures leave no half-finished state, essential for operations like money transfers.

topics.label: Isolation Levels
topics.desc: The trade-off between concurrency and correctness across Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, and Serializable, defined by which anomalies (dirty, non-repeatable, phantom reads) they permit.

topics.label: Locking & Deadlocks
topics.desc: Coordinating concurrent access via shared and exclusive locks and multi-version concurrency control (MVCC), and the deadlocks that arise when transactions wait on each other, detected and broken by aborting a victim.

topics.label: Constraints
topics.desc: Declarative rules the database enforces on data: NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK, and DEFAULT, pushing validation into the schema so invalid rows can never be stored.

topics.label: Referential Integrity
topics.desc: Guaranteeing foreign keys always point to existing rows, with ON DELETE and ON UPDATE actions like CASCADE, RESTRICT, and SET NULL governing what happens to dependents.

topics.label: When to Use NoSQL
topics.desc: The rationale for non-relational stores: flexible schemas, horizontal scale, and access-pattern-driven design, weighed against losing joins and strong consistency that relational engines provide.

topics.label: Document Stores
topics.desc: Schema-flexible databases storing self-contained JSON-like documents, led by MongoDB, that suit nested, evolving data and let you query without joins by embedding related data.

topics.label: Key-Value Stores
topics.desc: The simplest model mapping keys to opaque values for extreme speed and scale, exemplified by Redis in memory and AWS DynamoDB as a managed store, ideal for caches and sessions.

topics.label: Wide-Column Stores
topics.desc: Column-family databases like Apache Cassandra and HBase that store sparse, partitioned rows for massive write throughput and linear scale across clusters, tuned to known query patterns.

topics.label: Graph & Vector DBs
topics.desc: Stores built around relationships and similarity: Neo4j with its Cypher language for traversing node-and-edge graphs, and vector databases (Pinecone, pgvector, Qdrant) for embedding search powering RAG.

topics.label: BASE, CAP & Consistency
topics.desc: The distributed-store trade-off: BASE (Basically Available, Soft state, Eventually consistent) versus ACID, and the CAP theorem forcing a choice between consistency and availability under network partitions.

topics.label: ORM Concept
topics.desc: Object-Relational Mapping that bridges application objects and relational rows, generating SQL from method calls, with the impedance-mismatch trade-offs and leaky abstractions it introduces.

topics.label: JavaScript ORMs
topics.desc: The TypeScript and Node ecosystem of data mappers: Prisma's schema-first client, plus TypeORM, Sequelize, and the lightweight SQL-like Drizzle, that model tables as typed objects.

topics.label: Backend Language ORMs
topics.desc: Mature ORMs across other stacks: Python's SQLAlchemy, Ruby on Rails' ActiveRecord, Java's Hibernate/JPA, and Django's ORM, each encoding the framework's data-access conventions.

topics.label: Query Builders
topics.desc: A middle ground between raw SQL and full ORMs, like Knex.js, that compose queries with chainable, type-safe method calls while staying close to the underlying SQL.

topics.label: Raw SQL vs ORM
topics.desc: The trade-off between ORM productivity and portability versus hand-written SQL's control and performance, including when to drop to raw queries for complex reports or tuning.

topics.label: N+1 & Loading Strategy
topics.desc: The classic ORM trap where lazy loading fires one extra query per item in a loop, versus eager loading that fetches relations upfront with a join or batched dataloader to fix it.

topics.label: Schema Design
topics.desc: Deciding the tables, columns, types, keys, and constraints that represent a domain, balancing normalization, query patterns, and future change into a workable database structure.

topics.label: ER Modeling
topics.desc: Entity-Relationship modeling that diagrams entities, attributes, and the relationships among them before implementation, producing the ER diagrams that map a domain to a schema.

topics.label: Relationship Cardinality
topics.desc: Modeling 1:1, 1:N, and N:M associations correctly in the schema, choosing where foreign keys live and when a junction table is required to represent many-to-many links.

topics.label: Schema Migrations & Versioning
topics.desc: Versioning the schema as code through ordered, reviewable up/down migrations run by tools like Flyway, Liquibase, Alembic, or Prisma Migrate, enabling reproducible environments and zero-downtime deploys.

topics.label: Seeding & Fixtures
topics.desc: Populating a database with baseline reference data or realistic sample records via seed scripts and fixtures, so development, testing, and demos start from a known state.

topics.label: Soft Deletes
topics.desc: Marking rows deleted with a deleted_at timestamp or flag instead of removing them, preserving history and references at the cost of filtering every query and growing tables.

topics.label: Cache-Aside
topics.desc: The lazy-loading pattern where the app checks the cache first, falls back to the database on a miss, and then populates the cache, the most common application caching strategy.

topics.label: Write-Through & Write-Back
topics.desc: Write-time caching policies: write-through updates cache and database together for consistency, while write-back (write-behind) buffers writes in cache and flushes later for speed.

topics.label: Redis & Memcached
topics.desc: The dominant in-memory data stores used as caches: Redis with rich data structures, persistence, and pub/sub, and the simpler, purely volatile Memcached for raw key-value speed.

topics.label: Cache Invalidation
topics.desc: The notoriously hard problem of keeping cached data fresh by evicting or updating stale entries on writes, including key-based versioning and the risk of serving outdated reads.

topics.label: TTL & Eviction Policies
topics.desc: Bounding cache contents with time-to-live expiry and eviction policies like LRU and LFU when memory fills, the levers that trade freshness and hit rate against memory use.

topics.label: Query & Result Caching
topics.desc: Caching the results of expensive queries or computed objects keyed by their inputs to skip repeated database work, with stampede protection to avoid thundering-herd recomputation.

topics.label: Session Storage
topics.desc: Keeping user session state in a fast shared store like Redis rather than server memory, enabling horizontal scaling where any stateless app instance can serve any request.

topics.label: Full-Text Search
topics.desc: Searching natural-language text by relevance using inverted indexes, tokenization, stemming, and ranking, far beyond SQL LIKE, whether via Postgres tsvector or a dedicated engine.

topics.label: Elasticsearch & OpenSearch
topics.desc: The distributed search and analytics engines built on Apache Lucene that power full-text search, faceting, and log analytics at scale, queried through a rich JSON DSL.

topics.label: Meilisearch & Algolia
topics.desc: Lightweight, developer-friendly search built for instant typo-tolerant as-you-type results, with self-hosted Meilisearch or Typesense and the hosted Algolia service for app search bars.

topics.label: Database vs Search Separation
topics.desc: Treating the database as the source of truth and a search engine as a derived, denormalized index kept in sync, choosing where queries belong rather than overloading one system.

topics.label: Object Storage
topics.desc: Scalable blob storage for files and media via an HTTP API, led by Amazon S3 and its compatible alternatives (MinIO, Cloudflare R2, GCS), the standard place for unstructured data.

topics.label: File Storage & CDN
topics.desc: Storing file metadata in the database while bytes live in object storage, using presigned URLs for direct client uploads and a CDN to serve media from edge caches near users (CDN depth covered elsewhere).
